Definition: from G303 and G2749; to recline (as a corpse or at a meal):--guest, lean, lie, sit (down, at meat), at the table.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to recline at table, the way people ate in the ancient world: when evening came, Jesus sat down with the twelve at the last supper, and at that table one of His disciples was leaning on Jesus' bosom, the one Jesus loved. It appears fourteen times, almost always at a meal — guests reclining, the sick lying down, and once a corpse laid out.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for reclining carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the table — Jesus eating with His twelve, and the beloved disciple leaning on His breast.
